newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Black says wants higher Fairfax stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Black says wants higher Fairfax stake.

text.p: Hollinger International Inc chairman and chief executive Conrad Black said on Wednesday he would like to raise the group's stake in newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd to 50 percent from 25 now if an inquiry into media ownership liberalised foreign ownership rules.

Black also said Fairfax would be interested in diversifying into free-to-air and pay television if the government also liberalised rules governing cross ownership of broadcast and print media businesses.

Black was asked by reporters after Fairfax's annual meeting just how much he would want to increase his stake to, if allowed. "Fifty percent," Black said, adding that U.S. accounting rules effectively punished companies which had higher than 50 percent stakes in their associates.
When asked if Fairfax would want to diversify into Australian free-to-air and pay television, he said: "In principle, yes, they are obviously growth industries."
Black also said Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd proposal for a merged PBL/Fairfax group was unlikely to succeed while he (Black) was a shareholder.
